CLAIMSET Bias of the occurrence probability in iETS odds-ratio and inverse-odds-ratio models, and a score-based occurrence error proxy
licence CC-BY-4.0; contributions C1, C2, C3, C4
exploration {"lab_record": "A16", "questions": 2, "hypotheses": {"total": 25, "supported": 14, "not_supported": 8, "inconclusive": 2, "revised": 0, "abandoned": 0, "open": 1, "from_exploration": 13}, "tests": {"total": 25, "supported": 14, "not_supported": 9, "inconclusive": 2}, "runs": {"total": 41, "confirmatory": 29, "exploratory": 12, "failed": 1}}

DEFINITIONS
D1 [method] iETS_I: Inverse odds ratio occurrence model (SB23, eq. 18): o_t ~ Bernoulli(p_t), p_t = 1/(1+mu_b,t), mu_b,t = l_b,t-1, l_b,t = l_b,t-1 (1 + alpha_b e_b,t) (multiplicative error) or log l_b,t = log l_b,t-1 + alpha_b e_b,t (additive error); in smooth: occurrence='inverse-odds-ratio' (C++ case 'i' in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h). [source B1]
D2 [method] iETS_O: Odds ratio occurrence model (SB23, eq. 16): p_t = mu_a,t/(mu_a,t+1), mu_a,t = l_a,t-1, l_a,t = l_a,t-1 (1 + alpha_a e_a,t) (multiplicative error) or log l_a,t = log l_a,t-1 + alpha_a e_a,t (additive error); in smooth: occurrence='odds-ratio' (C++ case 'o'). [source B1]
D3 [method] old error proxy: The proxy for the unobservable occurrence error that smooth uses (occurrenceError() in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h): v_t = o_t - p_hat_t, u_t = (1 + v_t)/2; iETS_O: 1 + e_a,t = u_t/(1-u_t) = (1+v_t)/(1-v_t); iETS_I: 1 + e_b,t = (1-u_t)/u_t. With an additive occurrence error the log of the same ratio is used. [source B1]
D4 [method] occurrence filter: The recursion that produces the one-step-ahead probability $\hat p_t$ from the occurrences $o_1, \dots, o_{t-1}$, the initial state and the smoothing parameter $\alpha$: $\hat p_t = f(\mu_{t-1})$ with $f(\mu) = \mu/(1+\mu)$ for [[D2:iETS_O]] and $f(\mu) = 1/(1+\mu)$ for [[D1:iETS_I]]; the state is updated on every observation through an error proxy $e_t$ computed from $o_t$ and $\hat p_t$, as $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + \alpha e_t)$ (conventional multiplicative error), $\log\mu_t = \log\mu_{t-1} + \alpha e_t$ (additive error) or $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + e_t)^{\alpha}$ ([[D16:ADAM multiplicative ETS update]]).
D5 [method] Croston's method: Croston (1972): SES on demand intervals q and sizes z, updated only at demand occurrences; probability forecast 1/q_hat. [source B2]
D6 [variable] stationary mean probability: Long-run mean of p_hat_t produced by an occurrence filter applied to o_t ~ Bernoulli(p) with constant p, after a burn-in; compared with the true p.
D7 [data] Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability: Simulated o_t, independent Bernoulli(p) draws with p fixed over time.
D8 [method] score proxy: Proxy proposed in this study: the score of the Bernoulli occurrence log-likelihood o log p + (1-o) log(1-p) with respect to the log of the state, at p_hat_t: e_a,t = o_t - p_hat_t (mu_a: iETS_O, iETS_G) and e_b,t = p_hat_t - o_t (mu_b: iETS_I, iETS_G). Additive error: log mu_t = log mu_t-1 + alpha e_t (a score-driven filter with unit scaling); multiplicative error: mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + alpha e_t). Derivation: derivations.md section 4. [source B3]
D9 [concept] zero-drift point: For an [[D4:occurrence filter]] applied to $o_t \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p)$, a value $x^*$ of the one-step-ahead probability at which the expected update of the state is zero: $h(x^*) = 0$ with $h(x) = E[e_t \mid \hat p_t = x]$ (additive error) or $h(x) = E[\log(1 + e_t) \mid \hat p_t = x]$ (ADAM multiplicative error); for the conventional multiplicative update the expected change of the state is $\alpha\mu_{t-1}h(x)$. It is stable when $h$ moves $\hat p_t$ towards $x^*$ on both sides.
D10 [theory] score-driven model: Observation-driven time series models whose time-varying parameter is updated by a scaled score of the conditional log-likelihood (generalised autoregressive score / dynamic conditional score models). [source B4]
D11 [theory] constant-gain stochastic approximation: Recursions theta_t = theta_t-1 + alpha H(theta_t-1, o_t) with fixed gain alpha; as alpha tends to 0 their iterates concentrate around the stable zeros of the mean dynamics d theta/dt = E[H(theta, o)] (the ODE method). [source B6]
D12 [concept] inversion bias: The upward bias of Croston's 1/q_hat as an estimate of the occurrence probability, from Jensen's inequality applied to an SES of the demand intervals; of order alpha. [source B7]
D13 [variable] bias of the occurrence probability: Stationary mean probability minus the true p, for an occurrence filter applied to Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability p; estimated by simulation with a batch-means Monte Carlo standard error.
D14 [variable] alpha-to-0 limit of the stationary mean probability: For a filter and a p, the intercept at alpha = 0 of the least-squares line of the stationary mean probability on alpha, fitted to simulations at small alpha values; compared with the zero-drift point.
D15 [design] random design over p and alpha: Pairs (p, alpha) drawn at random with a fixed seed: p uniform on [0.02, 0.98] and log(alpha) uniform on [log 0.001, log 1]; or values of p drawn uniformly on [0.02, 0.98], each simulated at a fixed set of small alpha values. Each cell: one simulated series of Bernoulli occurrences, filter started at the true value, burn-in discarded, batch means for the standard error.
D16 [method] ADAM multiplicative ETS update: The update of a multiplicative level under ets="adam" in smooth: mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + e_t)^alpha, i.e. log mu_t = log mu_t-1 + alpha log(1 + e_t) (adamGvalue() in src/headers/adamGeneral.h, case MNN); conventional ETS uses mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + alpha e_t). [source B9]
D17 [method] exponential score proxy: Proxy proposed in this study for a multiplicative occurrence error under the [[D16:ADAM multiplicative ETS update]]: $1 + e_t = \exp(s_t)$, with $s_t = o_t - \hat p_t$ for $\mu_a$ ([[D2:iETS_O]]) and $s_t = \hat p_t - o_t$ for $\mu_b$ ([[D1:iETS_I]]), so that $\log\mu_t = \log\mu_{t-1} + \alpha s_t$; in smooth proxyOccurrence='score' with ets='adam'.
D18 [method] multiplicative score proxy: The [[D8:score proxy]] used with a multiplicative occurrence error in the form $1 + e_t = 1 + s_t$, with $s_t = o_t - \hat p_t$ for $\mu_a$ and $s_t = \hat p_t - o_t$ for $\mu_b$; under the conventional ETS update this gives $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + \alpha s_t)$ (in smooth proxyOccurrence='score' with ets='conventional'), under the ADAM update $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + s_t)^{\alpha}$.
D19 [data] M5 subset: The 3,000 pre-registered M5 series (subset.csv, seed 20261029): daily unit sales, days 1-1,969, leading zeros removed, the last 14 days held out (SB23 section 5). [source B10]
D20 [method] iETS(M,N,N) flavours: adam(y, "MNN", occurrence=X, distribution="dgamma") in smooth (ADAM in Python), with occurrence X in fixed (F), direct (D), odds-ratio (O), inverse-odds-ratio (I), general (G) or auto (A, selected by AICc among the others); O, I, G and A each with proxyOccurrence "ratio" and "score", under ets="conventional" and ets="adam"; F and D once, conventional (the proxy does not change them): 18 methods named iETS_<X>_<proxy>_<conv|adam>. [source B1]
D21 [method] SBA: Syntetos-Boylan approximation of Croston's method: Croston's forecast times (1 - alpha_q/2); tsintermittent::crost(type="sba") with default settings. [source B8]
D22 [method] TSB: Teunter-Syntetos-Babai method (SB23 eq. 6), tsintermittent::tsb() with default settings; point forecasts only. [source B11]
D23 [method] HSP: Hurdle shifted Poisson filter, counter::hsp() (counter 0.3.0.41003 from github.com/config-i1/counter), with upper quantiles from side="upper" at each level. [source B12]
D24 [method] NegBin: Negative binomial filter, counter::negbin(), with upper quantiles from side="upper" at each level. [source B12]
D25 [variable] RMSSE: Root mean squared scaled error of M5: sqrt(mean over h=1-14 of (y - f)^2 / mean over the in-sample of (y_t - y_t-1)^2), per series. [source B10]
D26 [variable] sCE: Scaled cumulative error: sum over h=1-14 of (y - f), divided by the in-sample mean; negative values mean over-forecasting. [source B14]
D27 [variable] sAPIS: Scaled absolute periods in stock: |sum over j of sum over i<=j of (f_i - y_i)| over h=1-14, divided by the in-sample mean. [source B14]
D28 [variable] scaled pinball: Mean over h=1-14 of the pinball loss of the upper quantile at level tau (0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99), divided by the in-sample mean absolute first difference; also computed for the quantile rounded up (SB23 eq. 35). [source B10]
D29 [variable] coverage: Share of the 14 held-out days with y at or below the upper quantile at level tau; also for the quantile rounded up.
D30 [method] Wilcoxon signed-rank test: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the per-series differences, score proxy minus old proxy, zero differences dropped (scipy.stats.wilcoxon, zero_method='wilcox'), with Holm's correction over the comparisons of each test at the 1% level; the direction of a difference is the sign of the median non-zero difference.
D31 [method] MCB: Multiple comparisons with the best (Nemenyi test on ranks) by rmcb() of the Python greybox at the 99% level: mean ranks of the methods over series, with intervals; two methods differ statistically significantly when their intervals do not overlap. [source B13]
D32 [variable] sum of point forecasts: Per series and method, the sum of the 14 point forecasts of the held-out days; the score proxy minus the ratio proxy gives the direction in which the proxy shifts the forecast.
D33 [method] rounded-up quantile: The upper quantile of an iETS forecast at level tau rounded up to the next integer, ceil(q_tau), so that it is a value the count data can take (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, eq. 35). [source B1]
D34 [method] Wilcoxon test, rounded minus raw: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the per-series differences in scaled pinball, rounded-up quantile minus raw quantile, of the same iETS method and level; zero differences dropped (scipy.stats.wilcoxon, zero_method='wilcox'); Holm's correction over the 72 tests (18 iETS methods x 4 levels); the direction is the sign of the median non-zero difference.
D35 [variable] coverage deviation: Per iETS method and level tau: |mean over series of the coverage - tau|; compared rounded minus raw as D, with a 10,000-draw percentile bootstrap interval over series (seed 20261030) at level 1 - 0.01/72 (Bonferroni over the 72 method-level pairs).
D36 [method] information-scaled score proxy: Proposed, not implemented: the score proxy scaled by the inverse Fisher information of the Bernoulli log-odds, s_t = (o_t - p_hat_t)/(p_hat_t (1 - p_hat_t)), used in place of o_t - p_hat_t for mu_a (and its negative for mu_b), with the same conventional and ADAM ETS forms as the score proxy (1 + alpha s, and exp(s) - 1 under ets='adam'). E[s_t] = 0 at p_hat_t = p for any positive scaling, so the zero-drift property of the score proxy holds; after a long run of zeros (p_hat small, o_t = 1) s_t is about 1/p_hat, close to the reactivity of the ratio proxy. Scaled scores of this kind are the inverse-information scaling of score-driven (GAS) models (Creal, Koopman and Lucas 2013). [source B3]

CLAIMS
C1 [descriptive; principal; support: simulation E8 artefacts A17; assumes C31; uses C10, C5, C6, C7; strength high (author); planning confirmatory; outcome supported]
  On [[D7:Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability]] p, for every p in (0,1), as alpha tends to 0, the stationary mean probability of [[D1:iETS_I]] and [[D2:iETS_O]] with the [[D3:old error proxy]], under either occurrence error type, converges to the [[D9:zero-drift point]] of the filter, not to p: the bias of the old filters does not vanish with a small smoothing parameter.
  scope: data_type: simulated Bernoulli occurrence series with a constant probability | excludes: time-varying occurrence probabilities; smoothing parameters estimated from data | conditions: both occurrence error types, conventional ETS update; limit as alpha tends to 0, extrapolated from alpha in {0.004, 0.002, 0.001}
  extends B1, at eqs. 24-25, own earlier work: Svetunkov and Boylan (2023) define the iETS occurrence models and the ratio proxies of their unobservable occurrence error (eqs. 24-25), the old error proxy of this paper.
  test: deterministic; tolerance 0.02; refutation 0.05; sample fixed by the design file; one run, no interim analysis; supported if a < tolerance and b < tolerance and c < tolerance and d < tolerance; not supported if a > refutation or b > refutation or c > refutation or d > refutation; verdict computed

C9 [formal; supporting; support: formal_proof E26, empirical_quant E5; verification unchecked; planning confirmatory; outcome supported]
  For every p in (0,1), with o ~ Bernoulli(p) and the one-step-ahead probability equal to p, the [[D3:old error proxy]] has a non-zero expected value: $E[1+e_a] = 2 - p + (1-p)^2/(1+p) > 1$ and $E[1+e_b] = 1 + p + p^2/(2-p) > 1$ for the multiplicative error, and $E[\log(1+e_a)] = -E[\log(1+e_b)]$ is positive below one half, zero at one half and negative above it for the additive error.
  scope: conditions: o ~ Bernoulli(p), p in (0,1); one-step-ahead probability equal to the true probability
  extends B1, at eqs. 24-25, own earlier work: Svetunkov and Boylan (2023) define the iETS occurrence models and the ratio proxies of their unobservable occurrence error (eqs. 24-25), the old error proxy of this paper.
  test: formal; sample one run; grid of p from 0.0005 to 0.9995 in steps of 0.0005; supported if u < 1 and c < 1; not supported if c > 0; verdict computed
C10 [formal; supporting; support: formal_proof E27, empirical_quant E6; uses C9; verification unchecked; planning confirmatory; outcome supported]
  For every p in (0,1), the [[D4:occurrence filters]] with the [[D3:old error proxy]] have a unique stable [[D9:zero-drift point]]: $1 - \sqrt{1-p} < p$ for [[D1:iETS_I]] and $\sqrt{p} > p$ for [[D2:iETS_O]] with multiplicative error, and for both models with additive error the root of $p\log\frac{x}{2-x} + (1-p)\log\frac{1+x}{1-x} = 0$, strictly between p and one half.
  scope: conditions: o ~ Bernoulli(p), p in (0,1); expected update of the state given the one-step-ahead probability
  extends B1, at eqs. 24-25, own earlier work: Svetunkov and Boylan (2023) define the iETS occurrence models and the ratio proxies of their unobservable occurrence error (eqs. 24-25), the old error proxy of this paper.
  test: formal; sample one run; grid of p from 0.0005 to 0.9995 in steps of 0.0005; supported if u < 1 and c < 1; not supported if c > 0; verdict computed
C11 [formal; supporting; support: formal_proof E28, empirical_quant E7; verification unchecked; planning confirmatory; outcome supported]
  The [[D8:score proxy]], $o - \hat p$ for [[D2:iETS_O]] and $\hat p - o$ for [[D1:iETS_I]], is the score of the Bernoulli occurrence log-likelihood with respect to the log of the state, has the true probability p as its unique stable [[D9:zero-drift point]] for every p in (0,1), and keeps a multiplicatively updated state positive for every alpha in (0,1].
  scope: conditions: o ~ Bernoulli(p), p in (0,1); alpha in (0,1]
  extends B3: Creal, Koopman and Lucas (2013) define score-driven filters, which update a time-varying parameter by the scaled score of the observation density.
  test: formal; sample one run; grid of p from 0.0005 to 0.9995 in steps of 0.0005; supported if u < 1 and c < 1; not supported if c > 0; verdict computed

C13 [formal; supporting; support: formal_proof E29, empirical_quant E13; verification unchecked; planning confirmatory; outcome supported]
  Under the [[D16:ADAM multiplicative ETS update]] the occurrence filter is the additive filter with error $\log(1+e)$, so that its [[D9:zero-drift point]] is that of the additive old filter with the [[D3:old error proxy]], differs from p for every p in (0,1) with the [[D18:multiplicative score proxy]] (below p for [[D2:iETS_O]], above p for [[D1:iETS_I]]), and equals p with the [[D17:exponential score proxy]].
  scope: conditions: o ~ Bernoulli(p), p in (0,1); ADAM multiplicative ETS update (ets='adam')
  extends B9, own earlier work: Svetunkov (2023) defines the ADAM form of multiplicative ETS, which updates a level as mu_t = mu_{t-1} (1 + e_t)^alpha.
  test: formal; sample one run; grid of p from 0.0005 to 0.9995 in steps of 0.0005; supported if u < 1 and c < 1; not supported if c > 0; verdict computed
C31 [descriptive; supporting; assumption (theoretical, tested)]
  For a fixed p, the stationary mean of the one-step-ahead probability of an occurrence filter with a unique stable zero-drift point converges to that point as alpha tends to 0, as [[D11:constant-gain stochastic approximation]] gives under regularity conditions that are not verified for these filters.
C14 [descriptive; secondary; support: simulation E9 (E9.R801, E9.R803, E9.R802, E9.R804) artefacts A17; strength moderate (author); planning confirmatory; outcome not_supported]
  On [[D7:Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability]], the [[D13:bias of the occurrence probability]] of the [[D3:old error proxy]] filters does not keep a fixed direction at every alpha in (0,1]: with multiplicative error the bias has the opposite sign in 1 simulated cell for [[D1:iETS_I]] and 2 for [[D2:iETS_O]], and with additive error in 0.
  scope: data_type: simulated Bernoulli occurrence series with a constant probability | excludes: time-varying occurrence probabilities; smoothing parameters estimated from data | conditions: 200 random (p, alpha) pairs, p in [0.02, 0.98], log alpha uniform on [log 0.001, 0]; the wrong-direction cells have multiplicative error and alpha between 0.88 and 0.96
  extends B1, at eqs. 24-25, own earlier work: Svetunkov and Boylan (2023) define the iETS occurrence models and the ratio proxies of their unobservable occurrence error (eqs. 24-25), the old error proxy of this paper.
  test: deterministic; z 4; sample fixed by the design file; one run, no interim analysis; supported if a + b + c + d < 1; not supported if a + b + c + d > 0; verdict computed

Design: Run 1 and run 2: Forecasts: forecast_iets.py (Python ADAM, 18 iETS(M,N,N) flavours: F and D conventional; O, I, G, A with proxyOccurrence ratio and score under ets conventional and adam; Gamma sizes; holdout of 14 days; upper quantiles at 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99 with interval="prediction", side="upper", seed per series and model) and forecast_benchmarks.R (Croston, SBA, TSB from tsintermittent with defaults, point only; HSP and NegBin from counter with side="upper" at each level), both with 2 workers, on the rows of subset.csv; leading zeros removed (load.py). Run 3: evaluate.py direction on the two files. Each evaluation run writes series_measures.csv (RMSSE, sCE, sAPIS, scaled pinball and coverage at each level, raw and rounded up, per series and method) and summary_measures.csv (per method and measure: n, mean, sd, min, quartiles, max), registered as artefacts. No --holdout file is declared: subset.csv was drawn from the series keys only, and the exploratory M5 runs (RN22-RN31) read it only to stay outside its rows. Analysis: Per series, the sum of the 14 point forecasts, score minus ratio, for iETS_I and iETS_O under conventional and ADAM ETS (4 comparisons); predicted signs + (I, conventional), - (O, conventional), - (I, ADAM), - (O, ADAM). Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, zero differences dropped, Holm-corrected at alpha 0.01 over the 4; the direction is the sign of the median non-zero difference.

E23 [quant; design benchmark] Lab runs RN38 under plan PL34. Design: Evaluation: evaluate.py mcb, at code commit 237c71d2 or later, on the forecast files of runs RN32 (iets_forecasts.csv) and RN33 (benchmark_forecasts.csv) of PL29. Same test and rule as PL32 and PL33 except that the mean ranks and intervals of rmcb() are labelled by the method names in its output index: in RN37 they were matched to the names in alphabetical order while rmcb() returns them sorted by mean rank (NT11). A new plan rather than a correction, because a corrected plan keeps the deciding run of the plan it corrects (L16). The run writes series_measures.csv and summary_measures.csv. No --holdout file is declared: subset.csv was drawn from the series keys only, and the exploratory M5 runs (RN22-RN31) read it only to stay outside its rows. E26 [formal; foundation real analysis and the Kolmogorov axioms of probability] Derivation checked by lab runs RN6 under plan PL9. Design: Section 2 of derivations.md (artefact AR1) derives the statement; derivations_check.py old-drift verifies each identity with sympy and each inequality on 1,999 values of p in (0,1) (and of p_hat where it appears) with 50-digit arithmetic.
  s1 u = \frac{1 + o - \hat p}{2};\ \hat p = p \Rightarrow u = \frac{2-p}{2} \text{ w.p. } p,\ u = \frac{1-p}{2} \text{ w.p. } 1-p (by D3; definition)
  s2 E[1+e_a] = p\frac{2-p}{p} + (1-p)\frac{1-p}{1+p} = 2 - p + \frac{(1-p)^2}{1+p} (by s1; substitution)
  s3 E[1+e_b] = p\frac{p}{2-p} + (1-p)\frac{1+p}{1-p} = 1 + p + \frac{p^2}{2-p} (by s1; substitution)
  s4 1 - p > 0,\ \frac{(1-p)^2}{1+p} > 0,\ p > 0,\ \frac{p^2}{2-p} > 0 \Rightarrow E[1+e_a] > 1,\ E[1+e_b] > 1 (by s2, s3; algebra)
  s5 g(p) := E[\log(1+e_a)] = p\log\frac{2-p}{p} + (1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1+p} = -E[\log(1+e_b)] (by s1; substitution)
  s6 g(1-p) = -g(p) \Rightarrow g(1/2) = 0 (by s5; algebra)
  s7 g(p) > 0 \text{ on } (0, 1/2) (by s5, s6; numerical verification on 1,999 grid values with 50-digit arithmetic)
E27 [formal; foundation real analysis and the Kolmogorov axioms of probability] Derivation checked by lab runs RN7 under plan PL7. Design: Section 3 of derivations.md (artefact AR1) derives the statement; derivations_check.py fixed-points verifies each identity with sympy and each inequality on 1,999 values of p in (0,1) (and of p_hat where it appears) with 50-digit arithmetic.
  s1 h_b(x) = p\frac{x}{2-x} + (1-p)\frac{1+x}{1-x} - 1 = \frac{-2(x^2 - 2x + p)}{(2-x)(1-x)} (by D3, D9; substitution)
  s2 h_b(x) = 0,\ x \in (0,1) \iff x = 1 - \sqrt{1-p};\ \sqrt{1-p} > 1 - p \Rightarrow 1 - \sqrt{1-p} < p (by s1; quadratic formula)
  s3 h_b < 0 \text{ for } x < x^*,\ h_b > 0 \text{ for } x > x^*: x^* \text{ stable} (by s1, s2; sign argument)
  s4 h_a(x) = p\frac{2-x}{x} + (1-p)\frac{1-x}{1+x} - 1 = \frac{2(p - x^2)}{x(1+x)} = 0 \iff x = \sqrt{p} > p,\ \text{stable} (by D3, D9; substitution and sign argument)
  s5 \text{additive error: } h(x) = p\log\frac{x}{2-x} + (1-p)\log\frac{1+x}{1-x} \text{ for both models} (by D3, D9; substitution)
  s6 h \text{ has a unique root in } (0,1), \text{ stable, equal to } 1/2 \text{ at } p = 1/2 \text{ and strictly between } p \text{ and } 1/2 \text{ otherwise} (by s5; numerical verification on 1,999 grid values with 50-digit arithmetic)
E28 [formal; foundation real analysis and the Kolmogorov axioms of probability] Derivation checked by lab runs RN8 under plan PL10. Design: Section 4 of derivations.md (artefact AR1) derives the statement; derivations_check.py score verifies each identity with sympy and each inequality on 1,999 values of p in (0,1) (and of p_hat where it appears) with 50-digit arithmetic.
  s1 \ell = o\log p + (1-o)\log(1-p),\ \frac{\partial\ell}{\partial p} = \frac{o-p}{p(1-p)} (by D1, D2; differentiation)
  s2 \frac{\partial p}{\partial\log\mu_a} = p(1-p),\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial\log\mu_b} = -p(1-p) (by D1, D2; differentiation)
  s3 \frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\log\mu_a} = o - p,\ \frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\log\mu_b} = p - o (by s1, s2; chain rule)
  s4 E[e \mid \hat p = x] = \pm(p - x) \Rightarrow \text{unique stable zero-drift point } x = p (by s3, D9; linearity of expectation and sign argument)
  s5 e \in (-1, 1) \Rightarrow 1 + \alpha e > 0 \text{ for } \alpha \in (0,1] (by s3; bound)
E29 [formal; foundation real analysis and the Kolmogorov axioms of probability] Derivation checked by lab runs RN15 under plan PL16. Design: Section 5 of derivations.md (artefact AR2) derives the statement; derivations_check.py adam-ets verifies each identity with sympy and each inequality on 1,999 values of p in (0,1) with 50-digit arithmetic.
  s1 \mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1+e_t)^{\alpha} \Rightarrow \log\mu_t = \log\mu_{t-1} + \alpha\log(1+e_t) (by D16; logarithm)
  s2 \text{old proxy: } \log(1+e) = \log\frac{u}{1-u}: \text{ the additive old filter} (by s1, D3; substitution)
  s3 1+e = 1+s,\ E[s] = 0 \text{ at } x = p \Rightarrow E[\log(1+s)] < 0 \text{ at } x = p (by s1, D18; Jensen's inequality)
  s4 \text{iETS\_O: } p\log(2-x) + (1-p)\log(1-x) = 0,\ x < p;\ \text{iETS\_I: } p\log x + (1-p)\log(1+x) = 0,\ x > p (by s3; substitution; numerical verification on 1,999 grid values)
  s5 1+e = \exp(s) \Rightarrow \log(1+e) = s: \text{ the additive score filter, zero-drift point } p (by s1, D17; substitution)

WARRANTS
W1 [deductive; premises C1, C12] C12 shows the stationary mean of Croston's 1/q_hat converging to p as alpha tends to 0, and C1 shows that of iETS_I and iETS_O with the old error proxy converging to a zero-drift point different from p; the two biases therefore differ in kind: one vanishes with the smoothing parameter, the other does not.
W2 [abductive; premises C10, C21] By C10 the old proxy pushes the probability of iETS_O up and that of iETS_I down. iETS_G updates mu_a as iETS_O does and mu_b as iETS_I does, and its probability is mu_a/(mu_a+mu_b), so the two upward pushes on its states act on the probability in opposite directions. The M5 RMSSE of iETS_G under conventional ETS changed little with the score proxy (C21: not significant at the 1% level), unlike that of iETS_O and iETS_I. iETS_A selects among the iETS models by information criterion and inherits the same offset.
W3 [abductive; premises C5, C22, C20] By C5 the old proxy biases the probability of iETS_I under conventional ETS downwards, and on M5 the forecast sum of iETS_I rises when the score proxy replaces it (C20). A lower probability puts more mass at zero and lowers the upper quantiles. At 0.99 the lower quantiles of the old proxy gave a lower scaled pinball on most series and a better MCB rank, while their mean scaled pinball was higher and their coverage further below 0.99 (table T1 of E23).
W4 [abductive; premises C11, C21] After a demand that follows a run of zeros, with a small one-step-ahead probability p_hat, the old proxy of iETS_O gives 1 + e_a = (2 - p_hat)/p_hat, a jump in the state of about 2/p_hat, close to Croston's interval update; the score proxy moves the log of the state by o - p_hat, at most 1 (C11). A filter that reacts strongly after long runs of zeros adapts faster to changes in the probability, which may be worth more on non-stationary retail series than the removal of the bias; the RMSSE gains of the score proxy were large only where the old proxy's bias was large (C21).
W5 [abductive; premises C24, C22, C25, C26] NegBin and HSP rank better than every iETS model on the scaled pinball at 0.80, 0.90 and 0.95 whichever proxy the iETS model uses (C24, C22), and rounding the iETS quantiles up does not close the gap (C25, C26). The iETS models model demand sizes with a continuous Gamma distribution, NegBin and HSP with count distributions; the occurrence proxy changes the probability, not the shape of the size distribution.

LIMITATIONS
L1 [analytic_flexibility; affects C23; could_bias_magnitude; mitigation none] In the first MCB evaluation of the M5 forecasts, evaluate.py matched the mean ranks and intervals returned by greybox rmcb(), which are sorted by mean rank, to the method names in alphabetical order, so each method's rank and interval belong to another method and the counts of significant comparisons are not those of the planned analysis; the labelling was fixed in code commit 237c71d2 and the evaluation rerun on the same forecasts.
L2 [sampling; affects C20, C21, C22, C24, C25, C26; reduces_transferability; mitigation none] All 3,000 M5 series come from the stores of one retailer, Walmart, in three US states, over one period of 1,969 days.
L3 [model_specification; affects C1, C2, C4; could_bias_magnitude; mitigation partial] The convergence of the stationary mean to the zero-drift point as alpha tends to 0 is taken from constant-gain stochastic approximation without verifying its regularity conditions for the iETS filters (C31).

OPEN QUESTIONS
O1 [from C2, C21, C29] Whether the score proxy scaled by the inverse Fisher information of the Bernoulli log-odds, (o - p_hat)/(p_hat (1 - p_hat)), keeps the zero drift of the score proxy and the reactivity of the old proxy, and so improves the accuracy of iETS models, is not established.
O2 [from C1, C20] How much of the bias of the old error proxy the likelihood estimation of the occurrence smoothing parameter and initial level absorbs on real data is not established.
